model.front_pairs: Eight mix16B windows input+0..112 / secret+0..127 in pairs (0,16),(32,48),(64,80),(96,112), each with seed. acc starts at len * PRIME64_1, acc2 at 0; each pair step folds into (acc, acc2) with the partner window's input-word sum xored in: acc = (fold_a + acc) ^ (input[b]+input[b+8]), acc2 = (fold_b + acc2) ^ (input[a]+input[a+8]). Both accumulators are then XXH3_avalanche'd (0x61d8294..0x61d82d1)
model.middle_pairs: Pairs gated on len: (input+128/secret+3, input+144/secret+19) when len > 159; (input+160/secret+35, input+176/secret+51) when len > 191; (input+192/secret+67, input+208/secret+83) when len > 223. Equivalently the pair (i, i+1) runs while i+1 < len//16, so the i=14 window (input+224/secret+99) never runs even at len 240. Same cross-XOR idiom as the front pairs
model.tail: low64 = XXH3_avalanche(A + B); high64 = -XXH3_avalanche(A * PRIME64_1 + B * PRIME64_4 + (len - seed) * PRIME64_2), where A and B are the two folded trailing accumulators. The (len - seed) term is what the body computes (rsi = len - seed at 0x61d8435); the 128bits caller passes seed 0 so it uses len
model.trailing_pair: mix16B(input+len-16, secret+103) into acc and mix16B(input+len-32, secret+119) into acc2, with the seed NEGATED (low secret word minus seed, high secret word plus seed -- the opposite signs from every earlier mix16B), each xored with the partner window's input-word sum: A = (fold_a + acc) ^ (input[len-32]+input[len-24]), B = (fold_b + acc2) ^ (input[len-16]+input[len-8])

return_value: 128-bit hash as (low64, high64) in (%rax, %rdx). The Hash2x64 wrappers store high64 through their first out-pointer argument and low64 through the second

semantics.pair_loop_note: The middle loop runs pairs while i+1 < len//16: at len 240 (len//16 == 15) the i=14 window is skipped, and the trailing pair covers input+224 with secret+103, not secret+99
semantics.scope: Lengths 129..240 only, the len_129to240 helper at 0x61d80a0. Lengths 0..128 are reconstructed in PR #5578; the >240 hashLong helpers (0x61d8a60 / 0x61d9bc0) are delegation targets only and are out of scope here
semantics.seed_term: The seed is added to the low secret word and subtracted from the high secret word in the front and middle mix16B calls, negated in the trailing pair, and (len - seed) is multiplied by PRIME64_2 in the high64 term. The secretSize argument is never read

side_effects: The function writes no memory, calls nothing, and reads only [data, data+len) and the secret windows listed in the model. It uses only the red zone below the stack pointer (locals at -0x58(%rsp) after six pushes) and restores all callee-saved registers

tests.cases: 2,400 deterministic cases (lengths 129..240 cycled; 12 seeds including 0, 1, 2, PRIME64_1 and 0xffffffffffffffff). Transliteration vs independent loop-form reference: 0 mismatches. See result.json
tests.native_execution_check: During development the transliteration was checked by executing the extracted 1134 function bytes natively (mmap RWX + ctypes trampoline, leaf function, controlled input/secret buffers): 3,000 random cases, lengths 129..240, 8 seeds plus custom 192-byte secrets, 0 mismatches. Two harness bugs were found and fixed during that check (a truncated mmap return and a mis-encoded REX prefix that zeroed the seed); the committed cross-check is the Python reference, and the native execution is not an input to the generator
tests.oracle_check: The extracted bytes agree with the system libxxhash 0.8.2 oracle at the 128-bit entry points (XXH3_128bits / _withSeed, lengths 129..240): 0/40 mismatches unseeded, 0/40 seeded; the oracle is not an input to the generator
tests.published_anchors: No published test vector exists for this helper in isolation; the check values in check-values.tsv are computed values confirmed against the system oracle at the entry points
tests.unit_tests: tests/test_xxh3_len_129to240_128b115.py, 11 tests (check values, out-of-scope rejection, transliteration-vs-reference agreement over all boundary lengths, seed sensitivity, secret-window sensitivity, custom-secret agreement, binary grounding including the caller bodies, result regeneration)

unknowns: Whether any caller other than the two 128-bit entry points reaches this helper is not established beyond the whole-.text E8/lea scan (exactly two call sites, no lea references)
The >240 hashLong helpers at 0x61d8a60 / 0x61d9bc0 and the 64-bit len_129to240 variant at 0x61d7dc0 are delegation targets / siblings only; their bodies are not reconstructed here
No source-level rationale is claimed for the trailing pair negating the seed, or for the middle pair loop skipping the i=14 window at len 240; both are recorded as observed in the disassembly
